items.authored_reason: Small-chain MPO construction, commutator identity and a structurally independent dense Liouvillian solve test the exact finite-n theorem.
The Hamiltonian commutator, cubic bulk algebra and boundary relations are tested explicitly before the dense Liouvillian fixed-point cross-check.
Explicit S_n matrices verify upper triangularity, unit diagonal and full-rank positive NESS.
Minimal d=1+floor(n/2) and enlarged auxiliary contractions are compared entry by entry.
Independent epsilon-squared interpolation proves the upper degree 2n-2 and a nonzero leading coefficient.
Transfer normalization, one-point and two-point observables are cross-checked against the full density matrix.
The general doubled-auxiliary transfer prescription is independently checked through normalization and arbitrary one- and two-point Pauli observables.
The one-sided hopping vertex identity and bond-independent dense current verify the printed epsilon/2 current normalization.
All nine finite magnetization profiles and the isotropic analytical overlay follow from the printed transfer equations.
All nine finite current curves and the isotropic analytical overlay follow from the printed transfer equations.
The easy-axis current sequence tests the printed exponential insulating law.
The paper prints a closed current formula, its limiting coefficients and a maximum near epsilon=1.63.
Deterministic band-operation counts test the claimed O(n^2) cost without wall-clock noise.

Complete Eq. (7) substitution at r=m and r=m-1 audits the root-of-unity closure; the repaired diagnostic preserves a stable cutoff-index, hopping-parity and auxiliary-dimension discrepancy for fresh review.
The general amplitudes reproduce every entry of the printed 3-by-3 Delta=1/2 matrix for all plotted couplings.
The fitted finite-current error rate is compared with the two-leading-eigenvalue ratio, while the Perron expectation and finite bulk profiles test asymptotic flatness.
The easy-axis profile's coupling independence and the printed exponential current factor are both checked.
For arbitrary requested rank, a shifted triangular minor has nonzero diagonal entries certified by the printed isotropic or hyperbolic amplitudes.
Every printed lambda-to-zero isotropic amplitude is evaluated and compared.
The double commutator, both boundary identities and alpha normalization coefficient are independently checked.
Finite-size convergence toward the continuum cosine profile is measured over four chain lengths.
The paper prints the complete leading 1/n correlation kernel.
The paper prints weak-coupling current and profile formulas and the crossover epsilon star=2 pi/n.

direct_gap_statements: For m=3..8, the full Eq. (7) amplitudes leave the paper-named component at r=m nonzero, while the opposite hopping vanishes at r=m-1 and produces an m-state auxiliary space rather than H_(m+1).

root_cause.statement: The prose appears to shift the true cutoff from r=m-1 to r=m and consequently assigns both the wrong hopping parity and the wrong auxiliary dimension.

code_fault_assessment.statement: An earlier reproduction diagnostic incorrectly forced a singular same-index tau branch and called the result a label swap. That code defect has been removed; the repaired single-source Eq. (7) implementation now agrees with the full amplitude arrays and the paper's m=3 matrix.

checks.statement: A full-density calculation independently reproduces the finite transfer observables.
The discrepancy follows from an exact symmetry or direct symbolic substitution, not a fitted visual comparator.
Every symbol used by the discrepancy test is tied to the printed equation and paper-exact regime.
The full Eq. (7) gives a nonzero paper-named r=m component and an exact opposite-parity zero at r=m-1, without a discretization or fit.
